definitions_cited.admitted_timings: START (flow in the day's opening value), MID (half in), END (flow in the day's closing value, the served convention). Defined as the relink function in org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_DASHBD/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_IRPT_DASHBD~121/y1_place.py (re-implemented here), which restates the same formulas as the private scripts of worker 108 (class90.py, relink) and worker 111 (s2_read.py, relink), as filed in UNCLASSED_90.json method.return_test and CONTESTED_51.json measurements.closing_by_convention_in_the_51
definitions_cited.tolerance: 0.35 percentage points between the custodian gross return (custodian time-weighted return grossed up by fees over the daily-mean served value, the ~35 v2 construction) and the restated served return; TOL_PP = 0.35 in the same scripts; UNCLASSED_90.json method.return_test
definitions_cited.dollars_tie: each of the four items (beginning value, ending value, net additions, net gains) ties within max(1 dollar, 0.1 percent of the larger): UNCLASSED_90.json method.dollar_tie
definitions_cited.flow_days_tie: the set of days on which the custodian transaction rows carry an external flow (by return date, day sums above half a cent) equals the set of served flow days: as ~120 x1_crosstab.py dates_same; CONTESTED_51.json date_sets_ledger_vs_served
definitions_cited.what_dollars_and_flow_days_tying_means_h: the four aggregates tie and the day SETS are equal. It does not require each day's amount to reproduce; that stronger test (234 of 235 flow days, 50 of 51 segments, DB-b-142 as quoted in CONTESTED_51_MEANING.json) is reported, not made a condition. The one segment with a day that does not reproduce carries an administrative expense row; under either reading it stays RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING and TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED (both START and MID close).

superseded_tokens.why: END is the SERVED convention, and END closes in 0 of 51. So no segment's served return closes against the custodian's; what closes is a RESTATEMENT under START or MID. RECONCILES_YES would be read as 'our number matches'. It does not. Nothing served is relabelled.
superseded_tokens.reason_for_the_chosen_tokens: Each token carries RESTATED (what was done to the return) and OTHER_TIMING (the served timing, END, is not the one that closes), so a reader meeting the token alone cannot read it as the served number matching; the lead RESTATED also keeps the axis apart from the TIMING axis, whose name and values lead with TIMING. The negative says DOES_NOT_CLOSE rather than a bare NO, so it is not read as a label of disagreement with the served number (the served END closes in none of the 51; a segment whose only closing timing is END would also fall here).
superseded_tokens.alternative_rejected: RESTATED_CLOSE_YES and RESTATED_CLOSE_NO: a trailing YES or NO is the very shape the ruling objected to (a reader takes the last word and reads 'closes: yes' as 'matches'), and neither names the timing that is not the served one. Also rejected, CLOSES_ONLY_WHEN_RESTATED: false for a segment that closed under END and under START together.

value_meaning.RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING: the return restated under START or MID closes within 0.35 pp; AND the four dollar items tie; AND the flow-day sets are equal. It is never a statement that the served number matches: the served convention is END, and END closes in 0 of the 51
value_meaning.RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMI: the segment is in the domain and at least one of those three conditions fails: no restatement under START or MID closes, or the four items do not all tie, or the flow-day sets differ

axes.domain_membership_rule: a segment is in the domain when a two-sided dollar read (custodian point for the range against the served daily series) and a flow-day comparison exist for it; today that is the 90 segments of worker 108's table

axes.name: TIMING
axes.question: Which flow timing did the other system use?
axes.domain: segments whose restated return closes under another timing (RESTATED_CLOSE = RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING)

value_meaning.TIMING_START: exactly one admitted timing closes and it is START
value_meaning.TIMING_MID: exactly one admitted timing closes and it is MID
value_meaning.TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED: more than one admitted timing closes; the data cannot say, and that is the final answer for the segment, not a contest and not a class of disagreement

axes.claim_reason: a fit is evidence and not the custodian's statement (ruling), so the three named timings are inferred; TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED states a measured count (two or more timings close) and asserts no timing
axes.consumer_rule: a consumer rejects a TIMING_START or TIMING_MID row whose timing_claim is not inferred, and never reads TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED as a timing

mece.finding: MECE over each declared domain, by subtraction from the printed denominators, with 0 uncovered. 244 = 90 in the RESTATED_CLOSE domain + 154 outside it. 90 = 51 RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING + 39 RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING. 51 = 4 (exactly one timing closes: TIMING_START 3, TIMING_MID 1) + 47 TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED. Inside the TIMING domain the count of closing timings is 1, 2 or 3 (RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING requires at least 1, and a close under START or MID among them), so 'exactly one' (two values, TIMING_START and TIMING_MID: END is the served convention and cannot be the other system's timing, so it is no value) and 'more than one' (one value) leave nothing over; in the 51 the count is 1 or 2, END closing in none. The 185 classed: 154 are outside the RESTATED_CLOSE domain (no two-sided dollar read exists for them: their classes were set from event-date and day-count tests, UNEXPLAINED_244.json classes) and 31 (the accrual class) are RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING. The 8 unclassed are RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING. On the TIMING axis none of the 185, 8 or 39 applies (outside the domain: TIMING is asked only of segments that reconcile).

same_grain.finding: Every value is a property of ONE segment, the (account, start, end) range that is the 244 and the 90 and the 51. RESTATED_CLOSE is one segment's restated returns against one custodian point plus its own four items and day set; TIMING is read from the same segment's three restated returns. No value is a property of an account (86 accounts hold the 90 segments, so an account value would mix grains), of a flow day, or of a pool: the pooled median log ratio over 86 flow days in CONTESTED_51.json is a pool-level figure and is deliberately NOT used to place any segment.

intent_coherence.finding: One axis, one intent. RESTATED_CLOSE asks only whether a RESTATEMENT closes: whether the return, restated under an admitted timing other than the served one, ties to the other system with its dollars and flow days; it is measured. TIMING asks only which convention produced the other system's number and is inferred. What the CTO ruling (msg 5886) found: END is the served convention and END closes in 0 of 51, so no segment's served return closes against the custodian's, and what closes is a restatement under START or MID. The first axis therefore measures a restatement closing, NOT the served number matching, and the renamed values say so; the earlier RECONCILES tokens could be read as the served number matching, which is not the case for any of the 51. No RESTATED_CLOSE value says anything about which timing and no TIMING value says anything about whether the segment closes: TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED is not RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING (47 of 51 close when restated and cannot be timed), and RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING carries no timing. The label CONTESTED today mixes the two intents: it names a disagreement (the return does or does not tie) for segments whose only open question is a fact no record can state (the time of day), which is the break this proposal separates.
intent_coherence.evidence: CTO msg 5835 item 1 'only one is a disagreement'; CONTESTED_51_MEANING.json what_is_settled_for_all_51 / what_is_not_settled_for_all_51 (all four dollar items tie in 51 of 51, flow days tie in 51 of 51, the open item is the time of day).

state_coherence.finding: Which values one remedy does NOT move. (1) A custodian statement of its flow-timing convention moves TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED (47) to a stated timing and changes its claim; it moves no RESTATED_CLOSE value, and it leaves the 4 inferred values to be confirmed or contradicted, not re-measured. (2) A change of tolerance or of the return construction (fee base) can move a segment between RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING and RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING and between TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED and a single timing; it is the one remedy that moves both axes, and it is a ruling, not an observation. (3) A ruling that accrual-explained dollar gaps count as tying moves the 31 accrual-class segments from RESTATED_DOES_NOT_CLOSE_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING toward RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING and into the TIMING domain; this proposal does not make it. (4) The shared code table's class for the one expense row (cell DB-b-146) moves no value on either axis, because that segment is RESTATED_CLOSES_UNDER_OTHER_TIMING and TIMING_NOT_DETERMINED under either reading. (5) Reading more of the 154 (a two-sided dollar read) moves segments INTO the RESTATED_CLOSE domain; it moves no segment already placed. (6) Re-timing the 4 inferred values requires a segment-level read of the custodian's intraday series, which no record read shows.
state_coherence.evidence: CONTESTED_51_MEANING.json groups 1, 3, 4, 5 (what_would_close_it per group) and not_established; UNCLASSED_90.json classes (accrual rule; 13 of the 31 close with accrual scaling under END, 18 only under START or MID, quoted not re-derived); y1_place.py gap figures: START and MID both within tolerance in 47 of 47 NOT_DETERMINED.
